latest_nl_proof:
We prove the statement directly.

If d = 0, there are no variables and no polynomials to choose. Affine 0-space consists of a single point, the origin, so the empty family already has common zero locus exactly the origin. Thus assume d >= 1.

Let kbar be an algebraic closure of k, and write [d] = {1,...,d}. For each i, let V_i be the k-vector space of weighted-homogeneous polynomials in S = k[x_1,...,x_d] of weighted degree e_i. Because all w_j are positive and e_i is fixed, there are only finitely many monomials of weighted degree e_i, so V_i is finite-dimensional. Also, taking J = [d] in the hypothesis, at least d of the d integers e_1,...,e_d lie in Sigma([d]); hence every e_i lies in Sigma([d]), so each V_i is nonzero. Set Vbar_i = V_i tensor_k kbar, set Vbar = Vbar_1 x ... x Vbar_d, and let N = dim(Vbar) = sum_i dim(V_i).

For a nonempty subset J of [d], define
A_J = { i in [d] : e_i belongs to Sigma(J) }
and r_J = |A_J|.
By hypothesis, r_J >= |J| for every nonempty J.

Now fix a nonempty J subset of [d] and an element a in J. Consider
U_{J,a} = { x in kbar^d : x_j = 0 for j not in J, x_a = 1, and x_j != 0 for j in J minus {a} }.
This is isomorphic to (kbar^*)^{|J|-1}, so dim(U_{J,a}) = |J|-1.

For each i in A_J, choose one monomial M_{i,J} involving only variables x_j with j in J and having weighted degree e_i; such a monomial exists by definition of Sigma(J). Since every coordinate indexed by J is nonzero on U_{J,a}, we have M_{i,J}(x) != 0 for all x in U_{J,a}. Choose a kbar-vector-space decomposition
Vbar_i = kbar M_{i,J} direct sum W_{i,J}.

Define the incidence set
I_{J,a} = { ((g_1,...,g_d), x) in Vbar x U_{J,a} : g_1(x)=...=g_d(x)=0 }.
We compute its dimension.

First, if i is not in A_J, then every weighted-homogeneous polynomial of degree e_i vanishes on U_{J,a}. Indeed, if some monomial of degree e_i used only variables from J, then e_i would lie in Sigma(J), contrary to i not in A_J. So every degree-e_i monomial uses some variable outside J, and hence vanishes on U_{J,a} because all such outside coordinates are 0.

Next, if i is in A_J, write uniquely
g_i = c_i M_{i,J} + h_i
with h_i in W_{i,J}. For fixed x in U_{J,a}, the equation g_i(x)=0 is equivalent to
c_i = - h_i(x) / M_{i,J}(x),
because M_{i,J}(x) is nonzero. Thus, once x and h_i are chosen, the coefficient c_i is uniquely determined.

Therefore I_{J,a} is isomorphic to
U_{J,a} x (product over i in A_J of W_{i,J}) x (product over i not in A_J of Vbar_i).
Hence
(dim I_{J,a})
= (|J|-1) + sum over i in A_J of (dim V_i - 1) + sum over i not in A_J of dim V_i
= N + |J| - 1 - r_J
<= N - 1,
because r_J >= |J|.

Let pi_{J,a} be the projection from Vbar x U_{J,a} to Vbar, and let B_{J,a} be the Zariski closure of pi_{J,a}(I_{J,a}). Since the dimension of an image is at most the dimension of the source, dim(B_{J,a}) <= N-1. So each B_{J,a} is a proper closed subset of the N-dimensional affine space Vbar.

There are only finitely many pairs (J,a), so
B = union of all B_{J,a}
is again a proper closed subset of Vbar.

Because k is infinite, V(k) is Zariski dense in Vbar; equivalently, no nonzero polynomial on affine N-space over kbar vanishes on all k-rational points. Therefore the nonempty open set Vbar minus B contains some k-rational point G = (g_1,...,g_d) with g_i in V_i. These g_i are weighted-homogeneous of degree e_i by construction.

We claim that over kbar their common zero locus is exactly the origin.

First, 0 is a common zero, because each e_i is positive, so each g_i has no constant term.

Now suppose x = (x_1,...,x_d) in kbar^d is a common zero with x != 0. Let
J = { j in [d] : x_j != 0 }.
Then J is nonempty. Choose a in J. Since kbar is algebraically closed and x_a != 0, there exists lambda in kbar with lambda^(w_a) = x_a^(-1). Set
y_j = lambda^(w_j) x_j  for 1 <= j <= d.
Because each g_i is weighted-homogeneous of degree e_i, we have
g_i(y_1,...,y_d) = lambda^(e_i) g_i(x_1,...,x_d) = 0.
Also y_a = 1, and y_j = 0 exactly when x_j = 0, so y belongs to U_{J,a}. Thus (G,y) lies in I_{J,a}, which means G belongs to pi_{J,a}(I_{J,a}), hence to B_{J,a}, hence to B. But G was chosen outside B, a contradiction.

So no nonzero common zero exists. Therefore the common zero locus of g_1,...,g_d in affine d-space over kbar is exactly the origin, as required.
role_in_parent: Provides the actual degree-prescribed equations once the Hall-type semigroup condition has been verified.
statement_nl: Let k be an infinite field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_j)=w_j. Let e_1,...,e_d be positive integers. For each subset J of {1,...,d}, define Sigma(J) := { sum_{j in J} m_j w_j : each m_j is a nonnegative integer }. Assume that for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, at least |J| of the integers e_1,...,e_d belong to Sigma(J). Then there exist homogeneous polynomials g_1,...,g_d in S with deg(g_i)=e_i for each i such that, over an algebraic closure of k, the common zero locus of g_1,...,g_d in affine d-space is exactly the origin.

domain_restrictions: w_j is a positive integer for each j in {1,...,d}
e_i is a positive integer for each i in {1,...,d}
Sigma(J) consists of all integers representable as sum over j in J of m_j times w_j with each m_j a nonnegative integer (so Sigma(J) contains 0 when J is nonempty, though e_i are positive)
the polynomials g_i are required to be homogeneous with respect to the weighted grading on S
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given an infinite field k, a nonnegative integer d, positive weights w_1,...,w_d, and positive target degrees e_1,...,e_d, define S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_j) = w_j and for each subset J of {1,...,d} let Sigma(J) be the set of all sums of the form sum over j in J of m_j times w_j with m_j nonnegative integers. If for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d} at least |J| of the values e_1,...,e_d belong to Sigma(J), then there exist weighted-homogeneous polynomials g_1,...,g_d in S with weighted degree deg(g_i) = e_i such that after extending scalars to an algebraic closure of k, the common zero set of g_1,...,g_d in affine d-space is exactly the origin.
quantifier_order: for all weight vectors w_1,...,w_d of positive integers
for all degree vectors e_1,...,e_d of positive integers
assume that for all subsets J of {1,...,d} with J nonempty, at least |J| of the integers e_1,...,e_d lie in Sigma(J)
there exist homogeneous polynomials g_1,...,g_d in S with weighted degree of g_i equal to e_i for each i
such that over an algebraic closure of k, the set of common zeros of g_1,...,g_d in affine d-space is exactly the origin
